page: Microsoft Azure D64d_v5 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the DDv5 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 256.0 GB of dedicated system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly with the instance, offering 2458 GB of local SSD capacity. This configuration operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include any GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with the instance placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores. The Intel Xeon processor's support for AVX-512 vector extensions contributes to strong results in Passmark CPU extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Memory subsystem performance is also strong, particularly in large-block read and write operations, which register at 291.88 GB/sec and 134.9 GB/sec respectively. However, single-core performance remains average, as demonstrated by middle-tier results in stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D64d_v5 offers a high resource density, combining substantial compute power with a large local SSD. This makes it a viable option for workloads requiring high-throughput local storage without the overhead of external disk attachments. The instance is suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and software compilation tasks, which align with its strong multi-core and memory bandwidth profiles. Conversely, it is less optimal for workloads heavily dependent on single-threaded execution speeds or GPU acceleration.
